insight.title: Why You Catch Up Faster by Slowing Down
insight.subtitle: How reducing your speed helps you reach your goals sooner.

sections.text: To catch an object in orbit, you don’t aim at it and accelerate. You slow down. This drop in velocity lowers your altitude, which actually increases your speed relative to the earth below.

We treat deadlines like targets we must chase with force. But high-pressure acceleration clouds judgment. By lowering your intensity, you drop into a "lower orbit" where you can finally see the path clearly.
This is about efficiency, not laziness. When you stop rushing, you stop creating the mistakes that usually slow you down. You reach the destination sooner simply by refusing to chase it recklessly.
Try this today: When you feel rushed to finish a task today, pause for ten seconds to check your direction.
True speed is the absence of unnecessary friction.

news.title: Trump announces 2-week ceasefire in Iran : NPR
news.description: After Iran ceded to President Trump's demand to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Trump backed down from his threat of wide-scale destruction of Iran's civilian and military infrastructure.
news.why: Stopping the conflict reduces the risk of war disrupting your travel.

news.title: Oil Plunges as Iran Reopens Hormuz Under Two-Week Truce
news.description: Oil prices fell sharply and Asian stocks rallied after the United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, with Tehran allowing ships to pass safely through the Strait of Hormuz.
news.why: Falling oil prices mean you pay less to fill your gas tank.

news.title: India's central bank holds benchmark policy rates as Iran war raises inflation risks
news.description: India’s central bank needs to weigh growth risks and inflation pressures from the Iran war as higher energy costs and supply disruptions mount.
news.why: High interest rates limit new job opportunities and salary growth for you.

news.title: Japan relaxes privacy laws to make AI development easy
news.description: : Opting out of personal data use won't be an option because Minister says that's a 'very big obstacle' to AI adoption
news.why: Companies can now use your personal data for AI without your consent.

news.title: JBS meatpacking workers return to work at Greeley, Colorado plant after UFCW sellout of strike
news.description: Workers returned to the plant Tuesday after the United Food and Commercial Workers suddenly canceled their powerful three-week strike without any progress at the bargaining table.
news.why: Full meat production ensures your local grocery store stays fully stocked.

news.title: Greece among the largest electricity exporters in the EU
news.description: Deputy Environment and Energy Minister Nikos Tsafos said on Tuesday that in the year’s first quarter Greece was among the largest exporters of electricity in Europe, following France, Sweden, the Netherlands, and Germany.
news.why: Strong energy exports help prevent unexpected power outages in your home.
